simple.meaning: קֶסֶת (qeçeth) is a place-name in the Hebrew text (H7083). BibleIQ follows its 3 occurrences across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: This place appears in Ezekiel, beginning at Ezekiel 9:2. The surrounding context includes altar, Israel.

structuredEvidence.definition: properly, a cup , i.e. an ink-stand

firstOccurrence.englishText: Behold, six men came from the way of the upper gate, which lies toward the north, every man with his slaughter weapon in his hand. One man in the middle of them was clothed in linen, with a writer’s inkhorn by his side. They went in, and stood beside the bronze altar.

timeline.evidenceText: Behold, six men came from the way of the upper gate, which lies toward the north, every man with his slaughter weapon in his hand. One man in the middle of them was clothed in linen, with a writer’s inkhorn by his side. They went in, and stood beside the bronze altar.
The glory of the God of Israel went up from the cherub, whereupon it was, to the threshold of the house; and he called to the man clothed in linen, who had the writer’s inkhorn by his side.
Behold, the man clothed in linen, who had the inkhorn by his side, reported the matter, saying, “I have done as you have commanded me.”
